problem:
Find where the tangent to the curve $y=4x-{x}^{2}$ at the point  $(1,3)$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The tangent intersects the $y$-axis at
$($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}} $).$
worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4x-{x}^{2}.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =4-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
m={f}^{′}(1)=4-2(1)=2.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =2(x-1) \\ y & =2x-2+3 \\ y & =2x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2(0)+1 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,1).$
